<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**11** anchor(s) derived from **2** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **173** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1169d64f438e094b3a148e9ead8e565e895975b9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `44d201249c32da2ae91f640f0282c7224a56e59b` — the merge of head `dc6cf1526fecb07edba0e49fec53f3727fceab0e` into base `1169d64f438e094b3a148e9ead8e565e895975b9`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 44d201249c32da2ae91f640f0282c7224a56e59b && git checkout 44d201249c32da2ae91f640f0282c7224a56e59b
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 1169d64f438e094b3a148e9ead8e565e895975b9 dc6cf1526fecb07edba0e49fec53f3727fceab0e && git checkout -B drift-repro 1169d64f438e094b3a148e9ead8e565e895975b9 && git merge --no-ff dc6cf1526fecb07edba0e49fec53f3727fceab0e

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 1169d64f438e094b3a148e9ead8e565e895975b9
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

epic:#31527#3 · os-tesla · session_01L9qibzECS2npZFku4956Um

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dc6cf1526fecb07edba0e49fec53f3727fceab0e`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/migrations/entries/semantic/18.two-shipper-declared-override-own-slot.ts + packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-registry-hydration.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-lock-state.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-diff-delete-load.ts, packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol-meta-list-reads.ts

Inputs read: card #33131 (body and all 6 comments), this PR's body, file list and net diff against `main`, the epic #31527 red lines, ADR-0150 D4, and the check-runs on this head. Nothing was built or run. The two test files and the two changesets are outside ④ (the lane seat's ACCEPT at `TIER_DEFAULT`); they were read only to see what is pinned.

Check-runs on this head when the record was written: 26 completed `success`, 11 `skipped`, none failed. Still running, so not judged here: `Build Core`, `Test Core (1/8)` to `(8/8)`, `Type Check · workspace`, `Type Check UI`, `Test UI (1/16)` to `(16/16)`. The PASS below is the design judgment plus the completed gates; the test shards that carry this PR's pins have not answered yet, and a red shard overrides this record.

Findings: 0 must-fix, 1 should-fix (S1), 4 nits (N1 to N4).

### ① Derived judgments

Each accept-set or surface change the diff implies, read from the tree:

1. **Read door, six sealed types** (`declinesStoredRow`, `protocol-lock-state.ts`): a pair's declared override of a page, app, dataset, doc, book or mapping is no longer declined when its base is not the first-registered shipper. **Right.** The row is still admitted only by `isServedOverrideRowOf` (pair binding by column, the body names the base, overridable type), now asked of the owner and of every shipper, exactly as the flow and action branches already ask. The door has no address, so I checked each caller that passes a row: the by-name read and the layered read reach a pair row only through `servedOverlayRowCandidates` for the address's own package (`overrideOf` must equal the address), the scoped list only through that package's pairs as stand-ins, `listServedOverrides` only through the base's own candidates, and `servedRowHolderOf` drops pair rows before it counts. None of them can serve beta's row at alpha's address, including when both packages share one App pair (the candidate holds only when the body names the address's package).
2. **Read door, the name-only question** (no row passed: `isStoredEntryOfDeclinedName`, `storedRowDeclined`): **unchanged.** With no row the new expression answers `true` for a sealed name, as the old one did.
3. **Read naming no package, sealed types, two holders**: **unchanged, right.** `packagelessContentPackage` answers `null` when several packages ship the name and no stored row is bound to one, so the pair row is not a candidate; for page, app, book, mapping and dataset the registry's `resolveItem` refuses a two-holder name before any layer is read. With one holder disabled the bare read now serves the enabled holder's own override where it served its shipped item, the same answer flow and action already give. Not pinned (N1).
4. **Boot census** (`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`): the six sealed types join flow and action on `someShipperOf`. **Right**, and required by triage note 6863797155. `someShipperOf` asks owner-then-every-shipper, the same question as the door, so door and census cannot disagree for these eight types. A stranger's row declaring a holder is still named (not the base's pair).
5. **Env-wide list filter** (`protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`): the flow/action gate is gone. What that changes for a type that was not in the gate: only an item whose own binding is not a shipper, of a name two or more packages ship, that `isServedOverrideRowOf` accepts as one shipper's declared override. That is reachable for the other overridable types only (the six sealed types, dashboard, report, email template, view, translation); every non-overridable type fails the predicate and keeps its entry, and a name with zero or one shipper never enters the branch. The dropped entry is a second copy of a row the merge has already served in its base's slot (`servedStoredRow`, same predicate), so no override leaves the list. **Right.** The bundle arm is new and correct in polarity: `baseAddressServesMember` is true for a pair-bound item only when the base does not ship that member, so the row is dropped only at a member the declared base ships and a pair's added member is kept, the same rule the sole-shipper branch applies.
6. **Registry envelope** (`declaredOverrideBaseOf`, `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`): a pair's declared override is registered under its declared base's artifact envelope. In effect this moves one type: of the overridable types, view returns earlier (`anotherPackageShips`), flow takes no envelope, and the nine types in `BORROWED_ENVELOPE_DECLINED_TYPES` still return before registration because the envelope is not the pair's own either way. So it is the action registry face (and translation, which cannot have two shippers). **Right**, and it now agrees with the registry's own `overlaySlotBinding` rule for a pair row (the holder its `overrides.package` declares).
7. **No export, no schema key, no stored-row shape** moves. **Right**: the one new function is module-private and `TWO_HOLDER_PAIR_SLOT_TYPES` was module-private.

Red lines: (1) no new predicate and no new door, so resolution is not loosened; (2) no answer in the changed code reads registration order any more, and no slot serves a row that does not name it; (3) see ④ for the one-holder reading of each file.

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: `minor`, with `Metadata-protocol: semantic`. A kind takes at least `minor` on the package the diff moves. **Matches.** (The #32613 changeset for the same step on flow and action declared `none` and `patch`; `semantic` here is the more careful reading, since which address serves an authored override changes.)
- `@objectstack/spec`: `patch`, `Metadata-protocol: none`, for the semantic entry alone. **Matches.**
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` is on the PR body and on the changeset, with the BREAKING banner, the FROM and TO readings, the one-line fix for a reader and the `adr-0087: registered` marker. `Check Changeset` and the lint gates that carry the ADR-0087 registration check are green. **Accepted**, with N2 on the value.

### ③ Boundary flags

`open_questions` in the os-dev-report (6868708766) is empty. The four deviations:

1. **Item 2 fixed although the list did not drop the override.** Answered: accepted. The card's condition was written before the measurement; what was measured (the override listed a second time under the first-registered package) is the same wrong answer item 3 has, and triage's own item-4 note names that family as red line 2. The fix removes a type gate from a filter already reviewed under #32613 and adds only the bundle arm judged in ① 5.
2. **Items 4 and 5 carried.** Answered: accepted. The PR says `Refs`, the card stays open, and the card itself orders them last. They live in `pairRowOnAddress` and `pairMemberWithheldAt`, which this diff does not touch.
3. **Census widening limited to flow, action and the six sealed types.** Answered: accepted, and it is not a real limit: no other sealed type is overridable, so the owner-only branch can never accept a pair row (N4).
4. **Two early card reads through `gh api` instead of MCP.** Reads only; no contract effect. Noted for the seat.

Nothing is escalated.

### ④ Design judgment

**`18.two-shipper-declared-override-own-slot.ts` (hits).** Against ADR-0150 D4: the row "registry overlay slot (ADR-0005): an overlay binds to the (package, name) it customizes, so overlaying one package's item never shadows another's" is what the entry's `reason` states and what the four implementing files do. Against its first consumer (the chain's TODO printer): the shape satisfies `SemanticMigration`, no `conversionIds` and no `relevantWhen` is correct (no stored row changes shape, and no question over one stack can see two installed packages), and the `replacement` is a real instruction (keep the override in the pair, read by package). Two wording findings:

- **S1 (should-fix).** `surface` says "a declared .custom override of one or both" and lists "the registry's item at each package" for an action. `acceptanceCriteria`, the changeset and every new pin cover one overridden holder only. With both overridden, the registry still holds one bare slot per name (`registry.ts`, `overlaySlotBinding` header: "The registry still stores ONE bare slot per name"), and the hydrator writes each override row into it in turn, so by my reading `getPackageScopedItem` answers the last-hydrated holder's override and the other holder's shipped action. That is never another package's row, and it is better than `main` (where the last row always sat under the first shipper), but it is one holder's override missing from the registry face, decided by hydration order, and card item 3 asks for exactly this face to be pinned. This is a reading of the code, not a measurement. Fix: add the both-overridden pin for `getPackageScopedItem` (both registration orders, both save orders); if it shows the shipped body, either fix it or say so in the entry and changeset and carry it on the card beside items 4 and 5.
- **N3 (nit).** `acceptanceCriteria` says the env-wide list "holds exactly one entry per package". For an email template a pair's added locale is a further entry, kept on purpose (the changeset says so; the entry does not).

**`protocol-registry-hydration.ts`.** The docblock holds sentence by sentence against the code: unbound, self-declared, undeclared and non-shipping declarations all answer `undefined`; "no shipper is picked" is true because the only candidate is the base the row's own body names, and it must both ship the name and pass the one predicate on the row's column binding. A package-less row cannot enter (`boundPackageOf` first), so the ruling 6817768147 sentence beside it ("never a pick between two") is untouched. One holder: `getArtifactItem` at the pair's id finds no local composite and scans to the sole shipper; at the base's id it returns that same composite, so the envelope is the same object and the answer cannot move (red line 3). Tried to break it with a bundle member the declared base does not ship (the lookup at the base would fall to another shipper's member): not reachable, because email template is the only bundle type and it returns at `declinesBorrowedEnvelope` before registration.

**`protocol-lock-state.ts`.** The code agrees with its comments. One holder: owner and shipper set name the same package, so the answer is the old one. The final `return true` is the old expression's value for every remaining type. N-level only: the method's contract docblock (`protocol.ts`, which the body names as its contract) and the `SEALED_ROW_SERVED_OVERRIDE_TYPES` header still say "the shipping package's declared override" in the singular; neither file is in the diff, and the sentence stays true per shipper, so this is a nit for a later touch, not a finding on this diff.

**`protocol-diff-delete-load.ts`.** The comment matches the code and the door (① 4). The kept ruling sentence in this file ("asked through the DOOR's own predicate") is respected: the census calls the same predicate through `someShipperOf`.

- **N4 (nit).** `perShipperType` is now a distinction without an effect: for any type outside flow, action and the six, `isServedOverrideRowOf` is false on either branch (sealed and overridable are exactly those eight). Calling `someShipperOf` for every type would remove the flag and the import.

**`protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`.** The comment matches the code (① 5). One holder: the changed branch is the two-or-more-shippers one only. Answer to the question asked of this review, whether dropping the gate changes any list for a type that was not in it: yes, by design and only as described in ① 5; I found no entry it drops that is not already served in its base's slot.

Remaining nits:

- **N1 (nit).** The comment this PR removes from `main` said moving the sealed types "changes what a read naming no package answers for each of them, which is measured and pinned" on this card. The new pins read each holder's address and the env-wide list; the bare by-name read (two holders: the 409; one disabled: the enabled holder's override) is not pinned. By my reading it is correct (① 3).
- **N2 (nit).** Item 1 makes a stored row that the reads declined served, and the census stop naming it; #32552 declared the same kind of change `yes (widening)`, #32613 declared it `no (narrowing)`. `yes (narrowing)` would state both directions. The level is `minor` either way, so nothing ships differently.

Observation outside this diff, for items 4 and 5 (not graded): the kept bundle entry in ① 5 (a pair's added locale of beta's template, at a member alpha ships) still goes through the list's envelope step with the pair's id, which falls to another shipper's artifact of that member. `main` kept that entry too, so this PR does not change it; it belongs with the member-withholding work the card carries.
